profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility is located at 215 East Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85013, per public property records; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites, treating those specifications as commercially site-dependent rather than public data.

Phoenix's data center growth has drawn sustained scrutiny of Arizona Public Service and Salt River Project, the two utilities serving the Valley. APS has said it received 19 gigawatts of electrical service requests from data centers and large commercial users it currently cannot serve, with individual requests now averaging about 500 megawatts each; data center peak demand has grown roughly 100 times faster than all other APS customer categories combined, even as average residential electricity use fell about 5% over the same period. APS filed for a nearly 14% residential rate increase expected no earlier than July 2026, and SRP raised rates in November 2025, including a 50% increase in fixed monthly charges for single-family homes.

reading.body:
This Lumen facility in Phoenix is a carrier-neutral colocation site operated as part of a 175-plus-facility network rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen does not publish per-building power capacity, square footage, or cabinet specifications for any of its sites, treating these figures as commercially confidential. The operator's standard cabinet power ranges from 3 to 15 kilowatts per cabinet, which differs from the 30 to 50 kilowatt densities typical of AI training infrastructure and suggests this facility targets network and enterprise tenants rather than large-scale model training.

Arizona has received 19 gigawatts of unserved electrical requests from data centers and large commercial users, with individual requests now averaging 500 megawatts. Data center peak demand has grown roughly 100 times faster than all other customer categories in the utility area serving Phoenix. This scarcity has moved the state's two major utilities, Arizona Public Service and Salt River Project, to file rate increases, with APS seeking nearly 14% higher residential rates and SRP having raised fixed monthly charges by 50% for single-family homes in November 2025.

Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, of which only four publish power capacity figures totaling 512 megawatts. Without published specifications from Lumen for this Phoenix site, its actual power footprint and AI relevance cannot be determined from operator disclosure. The facility's rank by published megawatts is therefore a category artifact, reflecting only that four other Arizona sites have chosen to disclose figures at all.
